firms.name: Advent International
firms.notes: Acquired AccentCare from Oak Hill Capital in 2019, its first move into home health and hospice.

firms.name: Alden Global Capital
firms.notes: Hedge fund known for aggressive cost-cutting at local newspapers; owns manufactured housing through its subsidiary Homes of America.

firms.name: Alpine Investors
firms.notes: Founder and lead sponsor of Apex Service Partners (est. 2019), the largest US residential HVAC/plumbing/electrical platform.

tags.description: Oct 2023 ~$3.4B single-asset continuation-fund transaction for Apex (among the largest in PE history) let Alpine return capital to investors while retaining the asset; in May 2026 Apollo Funds took a ~$2B minority stake at a $10B valuation, capitalizing the rollup further.

firms.name: Amherst Holdings
firms.notes: Runs the Main Street Renewal single-family rental platform; manages roughly $20B.

firms.name: Apollo Global Management
firms.notes: Acquired Cox Media Group's TV and radio stations in 2019.

firms.name: Ares Management
firms.notes: Co-majority owner of Aspen Dental Management (with Leonard Green & Partners; American Securities holds a minority stake).

firms.name: Bain Capital
firms.notes: Co-led (with Thomas H. Lee Partners) the 2008 leveraged buyout of Clear Channel, later renamed iHeartMedia.

firms.name: Blackstone
firms.notes: Took TeamHealth private in 2017 (its second time owning the firm). Co-investors include CDPQ, PSP Investments and Korea's National Pension Service.

firms.name: Blue Wolf Capital Partners
firms.notes: Created Elara Caring in 2018 (with Kelso & Company) by merging three home-health companies.

firms.name: Brookfield Asset Management
firms.notes: Acquired 135 manufactured-housing parks from RHP Properties in 2017; RHP retains ~5% and manages day-to-day operations.

firms.name: Cerberus Capital Management
firms.notes: Owner of FirstKey Homes, one of the largest US single-family rental platforms.

firms.name: Chatham Asset Management
firms.notes: Hedge fund; acquired McClatchy out of bankruptcy in 2020. Also controls Canada's Postmedia and American Media (publisher of the National Enquirer).

firms.name: Clayton, Dubilier & Rice
firms.notes: Acquired a 60% interest in Humana's Kindred at Home hospice/personal-care divisions in 2022 and rebranded them Gentiva; Humana held a 40% minority stake it is now divesting.

firms.name: Cortland Partners
firms.notes: Vertically integrated apartment owner/operator; ~80,000 units, #8 on the NMHC list of largest US apartment owners.

firms.name: ESL Investments
firms.notes: Eddie Lampert's hedge fund; controlled Sears Holdings from the 2005 Kmart merger through its 2018 bankruptcy, and now the ESL-controlled remnant, Transformco.

firms.name: Formation Capital
firms.notes: Senior-care-focused PE firm; owner of Consulate Health Care and an earlier (2007) co-owner of Genesis Healthcare.

firms.name: Fortress Investment Group
firms.notes: Managed GateHouse Media / New Media Investment Group, which merged with Gannett in 2019 to form the largest US newspaper chain. (Fortress itself has been owned by SoftBank and later Mubadala.)

firms.name: General Atlantic
firms.notes: Held a minority interest in ProSiebenSat.1's NuCom Group, the vehicle that took The Meet Group private in 2020 and folded it into ParshipMeet Group. ProSiebenSat.1 agreed on March 20, 2025 to buy out General Atlantic's minority stakes in both NuCom and ParshipMeet, ending the investment.

firms.name: GI Partners
firms.notes: Made a majority investment in ARS / American Residential Services in 2020; Charlesbank Capital Partners remains a co-owner.

firms.name: Global Growth (Eli Global / Greg Lindberg)
firms.notes: Greg Lindberg's holding company (branded Eli Global, later Global Growth) rolled up 100+ companies, including several insurers he controlled: Colorado Bankers Life, Bankers Life Insurance Company, Southland National Insurance Corporation and Southland National Reinsurance. Lindberg pleaded guilty in Nov 2024 to a ~$2B fraud/money-laundering scheme and was sentenced May 2026 to 12 years; the insurers went into rehabilitation/liquidation.

firms.name: Golden Gate Capital
firms.notes: Bought Red Lobster from Darden in 2014 (and formerly owned Payless ShoeSource, Eddie Bauer and others).

firms.name: Goldman Sachs
firms.notes: Goldman Sachs Alternatives (the firm's private-equity business). Acquired Sila Services in early 2025.

tags.description: In Sept 2025 the Nexstar Network (the largest plumbing/HVAC trade group) severed ties with all PE-backed members (~1/3 of its 800 members) over the roll-up model; Forbes cited Sila's 28-acquisition consolidation as a leading example of the consolidation the group rejected.
Acquired Sila Services from Morgan Stanley Capital Partners in early 2025 in a roughly $1.5B sponsor-to-sponsor deal including debt, a leveraged continuation of the HVAC roll-up.

firms.name: Great Hill Partners
firms.notes: Bought Gizmodo Media Group and The Onion from Univision in 2019, forming G/O Media.

firms.name: Greystar Real Estate Partners
firms.notes: Vertically integrated apartment investment manager and operator: the largest US apartment manager (~1M units under management).

firms.name: Gryphon Investors
firms.notes: Owner of Smile Brands (originally acquired 2016, sold, re-acquired 2024).

firms.name: Havenpark Capital
firms.notes: Utah PE firm that owns Havenpark Communities, a manufactured-housing operator.

firms.name: Hellman & Friedman
firms.notes: Controlling owner of Hub International since 2013; Hub reached a $29B valuation in 2025. Leonard Green & Partners and Altas Partners hold minority stakes.

tags.description: FTC consent orders (2022) required clinic divestitures and imposed prior-approval / prior-notice conditions on JAB's future specialty/emergency vet acquisitions (SAGE and Ethos matters).
Subject of a 2024 US Senate inquiry (Sens. Warren & Blumenthal) into consolidation and post-acquisition price increases at PE-owned vet clinics.
2023 recapitalization of PetVet used a ~$2.3B private loan to refinance over $3B of debt maturing from 2025.

firms.name: Leonard Green & Partners
firms.notes: Majority owner of Wrench Group (HVAC/plumbing/electrical) since 2019; TSG Consumer Partners and Oak Hill Capital took a minority stake in Nov 2022.

firms.name: Madison Dearborn Partners
firms.notes: Took Benefytt Technologies (formerly Health Insurance Innovations) private in an all-cash tender offer completed August 21, 2020 (~$410M, $31.00/share).

firms.name: Mars Veterinary Health
firms.notes: Family-owned CPG holding company; in scope as a holding company running a vet rollup.

tags.description: FTC required divestiture of 12 specialty/emergency clinics as a condition of the $9.1B VCA acquisition (2017), plus a 10-year FTC notice requirement.
Subject of a Nov 2024 US Senate investigation (Warren & Blumenthal) into Mars' impact on pet owners and veterinary workers.

firms.name: MGG Investment Group
firms.notes: Private credit manager. Already a principal creditor of Spark Networks SE, MGG-managed funds took 100 percent of the equity in January 2024 through a German StaRUG restructuring (the first such plan recognized in a US Chapter 15 proceeding), wiping out the existing shareholders.

firms.name: MHP Funds (Frank Rolfe & Dave Reynolds)
firms.notes: Investment funds run by Frank Rolfe and Dave Reynolds, who also run 'Mobile Home University' investor trainings; operate parks under the Impact Communities brand.

firms.name: New Mountain Capital
firms.notes: Owns two DSOs: Benevis/Kool Smiles (acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2020) and Western Dental / Sonrava Health (held since 2012).

firms.name: Oak Hill Capital
firms.notes: VetCor lead investor; co-owners Harvest Partners and Cressey & Company.

firms.name: OMERS Private Equity
firms.notes: Private-equity arm of the Canadian pension OMERS. Acquired TurnPoint Services from Trivest Partners in late 2020.

firms.name: Onex
firms.notes: Owner of SCP Health (formerly Schumacher Clinical Partners) since 2015.

firms.name: Pinta Capital Partners
firms.notes: PE group co-founded by Joel Landau; controls Genesis Healthcare through ReGen Healthcare (~93% equity). Genesis entered Chapter 11 in 2025.

firms.name: Pretium Partners
firms.notes: Founded and owns Progress Residential, the largest US institutional single-family landlord. Led by former Goldman Sachs executive Don Mullen.

firms.name: San Vicente Acquisition (Ray Zage / Tiga, James Lu / Joffre Capital)
firms.notes: Vehicle formed by James Fu Bin Lu (co-founder of buyout firm Joffre Capital), George Raymond Zage III (Tiga Investments) and J. Michael Gearon Jr. to buy Grindr out of Chinese ownership in 2020 for about $608 million, after CFIUS ordered Beijing Kunlun Tech to divest. Took Grindr public via a SPAC merger with Tiga Acquisition Corp on November 18, 2022 (NYSE: GRND) while retaining control; Zage and Lu together held more than 60 percent of the shares as of June 2025.

tags.description: 2025 ~$8.6B recapitalization merging Southern Veterinary Partners + Mission Veterinary Partners included ~$3B of secured debt.

firms.name: Stockbridge Capital Group
firms.notes: Founded YES! Communities in 2008; sold 71% in 2016 to a JV led by Singapore's sovereign fund GIC (with Pennsylvania's PSERS), retaining ~29%.

firms.name: Summit Partners
firms.notes: Led the 2018 buyout consortium for Sound Physicians (with Optum, Revelstoke and Silversmith).

firms.name: Sycamore Partners
firms.notes: Retail-focused PE firm; portfolio has included Nine West, Aeropostale, Staples, Belk and Talbots.

firms.name: The Carlyle Group
firms.notes: Former owner of HCR ManorCare (2007–2018). Its LBO ended in the chain's 2018 bankruptcy.

firms.name: The Portopiccolo Group
firms.notes: PE firm (Simcha Hyman, Naftali Zanziper) that rolled up ~100 nursing facilities under brands including Accordius Health, Pelican Health and Orchid Cove.

firms.name: Thoma Bravo
firms.notes: Software-focused PE firm; acquired RealPage in 2021 for ~$10.2B.

firms.name: TowerBrook Capital Partners
firms.notes: Co-owns Compassus 50/50 with the Catholic nonprofit health system Ascension (a PE/nonprofit joint venture).

tags.description: 2024–25 financial-press reporting documented persistent liquidity deficits at Thrive; the company engaged restructuring advisers and secured $350M+ of rescue financing.

businesses.name: AccentCare
businesses.platform_company: Home health + hospice provider (includes Seasons Hospice); Advent acquired it from Oak Hill Capital in 2019

businesses.name: Accordius Health
businesses.platform_company: Portopiccolo's nursing-home operating brand (part of a ~100-facility network incl. Pelican Health, Orchid Cove)

evidence.description: Investigative reporting (Axios, The New Yorker, Washington Post) documented steep staffing cuts and declining care after Portopiccolo acquisitions, including a Richmond-area (Henrico) nursing home where deaths doubled following the takeover, and a facility where some shifts had as few as two staff for 72 beds, with residents going days without care.

businesses.name: Apex Service Partners
businesses.platform_company: 100+ HVAC/plumbing/electrical brands; co-owners Partners Group and (2026) Apollo Global Management at a $10B valuation

businesses.name: ARS / Rescue Rooter (American Residential Services)
businesses.platform_company: ARS Network of HVAC/plumbing brands (Rescue Rooter, A.J. Perri, Blue Dot, Yes! and others); co-owner Charlesbank Capital Partners

evidence.description: Arizona AG consent judgment (April 2012, ~$395,000): resolved a 2011 lawsuit alleging ARS used false, misleading and deceptive sales tactics against (often older) consumers, including fake 'safety notices' to frighten buyers into unnecessary systems and official-looking solicitations, and undermined buyers' 3-day cancellation rights. ARS agreed to substantial changes in its sales practices. Predates GI Partners' 2020 ownership.

businesses.name: Aspen Dental
businesses.platform_company: 2nd-largest US DSO, 1,000+ locations in 46 states; co-owned by Leonard Green & Partners with a minority stake held by American Securities

evidence.description: California AG settlement (May 2026): Aspen agreed to $2M in penalties plus $300K restitution over alleged illegal corporate practice of dentistry and false/misleading advertising, with injunctive terms barring it from directing clinical practice or replacing practice-owner dentists of its choosing.

Massachusetts AG settlement announced Jan 5, 2023 ($3.5M): resolved a 2021 lawsuit alleging Aspen used bait-and-switch advertising, charging patients for exams/x-rays/screenings it advertised as free and claiming to accept all insurance when it did not accept MassHealth Medicaid. Aspen agreed to return up to $750K to affected patients.

businesses.name: Athene
businesses.platform_company: Athene Holding Ltd. (Bermuda): largest US annuity provider and a leading pension-risk-transfer (PRT) writer; wholly owned by Apollo since their 2022 merger

evidence.description: ALLEGED / PENDING: putative ERISA class actions (led by Schlichter Bogard LLP) allege that plan sponsors which transferred employee pensions to Athene annuities failed to select the safest available annuity provider, exposing retirees to added risk. The suits are pending and the allegations are unproven; the ERISA Advisory Council has heard comment on the fiduciary criteria used to vet PRT annuity providers.

Investigative and policy reporting documents concern about the Apollo/Athene model: annuity and pension-risk-transfer premiums are invested through Apollo's own credit platforms and risk is ceded to Bermuda-based reinsurance. Athene has reached at least 49 pension-risk-transfer deals with companies including Alcoa, AT&T and Lockheed Martin, converting roughly $53 billion of pensions covering about 535,000 people into annuities, moving retirement savings that retirees, regulators and economists say are exposed to higher and more opaque risk.

businesses.name: Benefytt Technologies (formerly Health Insurance Innovations)
businesses.platform_company: Online marketer of short-term / limited-benefit health plans and supplemental insurance products; renamed from Health Insurance Innovations in March 2020, taken private by Madison Dearborn in August 2020

evidence.description: Per the FTC, Benefytt (operating under names such as Health Insurance Innovations) and its partners ran deceptive websites targeting consumers searching for comprehensive, ACA-qualified health insurance, then charged them hundreds of dollars a month for products and services that often left them unprotected in a medical emergency.

FTC v. Benefytt Technologies: under a 2022 settlement, Benefytt was required to pay $100 million for consumer refunds, was barred from lying about its products and from charging illegal junk fees, and former CEO Gavin Southwell and former VP Amy Brady were permanently banned from selling or marketing health-care-related products. In March 2024 the FTC distributed $99,307,988 in refunds to 463,629 consumers who had paid Benefytt $1,000 or more between 2017 and 2022.

businesses.name: Benevis / Kool Smiles
businesses.platform_company: Medicaid-focused DSO behind the Kool Smiles clinics; acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2020 (prior owners: FFL Partners, then Tailwind Capital & Littlejohn)

evidence.description: US DOJ False Claims Act settlement (2018): Benevis and 130+ affiliated Kool Smiles clinics paid $23.9M to resolve allegations they billed Medicaid for medically unnecessary pediatric procedures: baby root canals, extractions and stainless-steel crowns on children (2009–2011), with dentists pressured by production-quota bonuses. Settled without admission of wrongdoing. Conduct and settlement PREDATE New Mountain Capital's 2020 bankruptcy acquisition (then-owners FFL Partners, later Tailwind/Littlejohn).

businesses.name: Bumble
businesses.platform_company: Bumble Inc. (Nasdaq: BMBL), which also operates Badoo. Blackstone bought a majority of the Badoo/Bumble group in November 2019 and controlled it through the February 2021 IPO; its stake has since fallen to a minority. Recorded as an ownership fact

evidence.description: At the completion of Bumble's February 2021 IPO, Blackstone beneficially owned roughly 57 percent of the outstanding economic interests and about 80 percent of the outstanding voting power. Blackstone entities have sold down since then; by mid-2026 they held about 22.4 million Class A shares, roughly 17.2 percent of the class, and had pledged shares against borrowings. Recorded as an ownership and control fact, not an allegation of harm.

businesses.name: Colorado Bankers Life Insurance Company
businesses.platform_company: Largest of several life/annuity insurers controlled by Greg Lindberg (with Bankers Life Insurance Company, Southland National Insurance Corporation and Southland National Reinsurance); placed into court-ordered liquidation effective November 30, 2024

evidence.description: US DOJ: Greg Lindberg pleaded guilty in November 2024 to conspiracy to commit offenses against the United States and conspiracy to commit money laundering, in connection with a scheme prosecutors valued at roughly $2 billion to defraud insurance regulators, policyholders and others. He was sentenced in May 2026 to 12 years in federal prison and more than $1.6 billion in restitution.

Per DOJ, from no later than 2016 through at least 2019 Lindberg caused the insurance companies he controlled to invest more than $2 billion in loans and other securities with his own affiliated companies, evading regulatory requirements meant to protect policyholders and concealing the insurers' true financial condition; he personally benefited by 'forgiving' more than $125 million in loans to himself from the insurers.

Colorado Bankers Life was placed into court-ordered liquidation effective November 30, 2024. A moratorium continues to apply to obligations not covered by guaranty associations (including cash surrenders, transfers, policy loans and interest on annuity accounts), and no interest has been credited on annuity accounts since the liquidation date. Lindberg's collapsed insurers left more than 200,000 policyholders, with claims paid out by state guaranty associations.

businesses.name: Compassus
businesses.platform_company: National hospice, palliative and home-health provider; owned 50/50 by TowerBrook Capital and the nonprofit health system Ascension

businesses.name: Consulate Health Care
businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US nursing-home providers, concentrated in Florida

evidence.description: False Claims Act case brought by whistleblower nurse Angela Ruckh: a federal jury found Consulate liable for 'upcoding', billing Medicare/Medicaid for medically unnecessary and inflated therapy. The judgment reached ~$258M; after appeals and six affiliated entities' bankruptcy filings, DOJ ultimately settled the judgment for $4.5M.

An analysis found a web of related companies made Consulate-owned nursing homes appear 'cash-strapped': a related-party structure that moves money among affiliates while limiting the operators' apparent ability to pay judgments or invest in care.

businesses.name: Cortland
businesses.platform_company: Vertically integrated apartment owner/operator: ~80,000 units across ~240 communities

evidence.description: Named in the DOJ's RealPage case; Cortland was the first landlord to settle (Jan 2025), agreeing to stop using RealPage's rent-setting software and not to share competitively sensitive data with competitors.

businesses.name: Cox Media Group
businesses.platform_company: 14 broadcast TV stations plus dozens of radio stations; Apollo acquired the TV group for ~$3.1B and a majority of the radio group in 2019

evidence.description: Apollo's 2019 acquisition of Cox Media Group's TV and radio stations was accompanied by rounds of layoffs across the stations, both around the deal's close and in the years after under PE ownership.

businesses.name: Elara Caring
businesses.platform_company: Home health, hospice, behavioral and personal care across 16+ states; created in 2018 by Blue Wolf Capital and Kelso from a three-company merger

evidence.description: $4.2M DOJ settlement (May 2024): resolved False Claims Act allegations that Elara Caring billed Medicare for hospice services for patients who were ineligible for the hospice benefit because they were not terminally ill, and knowingly retained overpayments, over roughly six years.

businesses.name: Envision Healthcare
businesses.platform_company: EmCare (ER staffing) + AmSurg (ambulatory surgery); KKR's equity was wiped out in the May 2023 Chapter 11, now owned by former creditors

evidence.description: Envision's EmCare unit was a central driver of the US surprise-billing crisis. A Yale study (Cooper & Scott Morton) of 2.2M ER visits found out-of-network billing rates jumped sharply after EmCare took over hospital emergency rooms (at ~15% of hospitals out-of-network rates exceeded 80%), exposing in-network patients to large surprise bills.

KKR took Envision private in 2018 in a $9.9B deal financed with ~$7B of debt (~70% of the price). When the No Surprises Act (2022) ended its lucrative out-of-network billing model, the debt load became unsustainable and Envision filed Chapter 11 in May 2023, one of the largest PE-backed healthcare bankruptcies. KKR's equity was wiped out and creditors took control.

businesses.name: FirstKey Homes
businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US single-family rental platforms, owned by Cerberus Capital Management

businesses.name: Fortitude Re
businesses.platform_company: Bermuda-based reinsurer of AIG's legacy life & retirement and general-insurance run-off (~$30B+ of reserves); acquired Prudential's PALAC in-force variable-annuity block (~$31B). Recorded as an ownership fact: 'who really owns your legacy annuity.'

businesses.name: G/O Media
businesses.platform_company: Digital publisher (Gizmodo, Kotaku, The Onion, Deadspin, Jezebel and more), bought from Univision in 2019

evidence.description: Under Great Hill Partners' G/O Media, Deadspin's entire editorial staff resigned in Oct 2019 after the company fired the interim editor for refusing a 'stick to sports' mandate; the staff left to found Defector. G/O later laid off Jezebel's staff and, in 2024, sold off Deadspin (laying off all its staff) and The Onion.

businesses.name: Gannett / GateHouse
businesses.platform_company: Largest US newspaper company: 260+ dailies including USA Today; assembled via the 2019 GateHouse–Gannett merger. Now publicly traded (NYSE: GCI) after internalizing management ~2020

evidence.description: Fortress-managed New Media Investment Group (owner of GateHouse) merged with Gannett in 2019 to form the largest US newspaper chain, a ~$1.4B deal funded partly by a ~$1.79B loan from Apollo Global at ~11.5% interest. GateHouse cut roughly 200 staff in the first half of 2019, and cost-cutting and layoffs continued across the merged papers.

businesses.name: Genesis Healthcare
businesses.platform_company: ~175 skilled-nursing/assisted-living facilities in 18 states; originally taken private by Formation Capital & JER Partners in 2007; filed Chapter 11 in July 2025 (an insider sale to ReGen/Pinta was rejected by the court in Dec 2025)

evidence.description: $53.6M DOJ settlement (2017): Genesis resolved allegations it billed Medicare/Medicaid for medically unnecessary therapy and hospice services and provided 'grossly substandard' care with inadequate staffing, much of the conduct at acquired operators Skilled Healthcare and Sun Healthcare (2005–2013).

Genesis filed for Chapter 11 in July 2025 with more than $2.3B in debt, threatening care for residents across 18 states. Sens. Warren & Blumenthal and Reps. Goodlander & Welch opened an investigation into the PE-driven bankruptcy's impact on nursing-home and assisted-living residents.

businesses.name: Gentiva
businesses.platform_company: Largest US end-of-life care provider; carved out of Humana's Kindred at Home in 2022 (Humana retained a 40% minority stake it is now divesting)

evidence.description: $19.4M DOJ and Tennessee AG settlement (2024): resolved allegations that Gentiva entities billed Medicare and Medicaid (2010–Feb 2020) for hospice services for patients who were not terminally ill and then improperly concealed or avoided repaying those claims; separately, its Alabama segment SouthernCare New Beacon paid kickbacks to a consulting physician to induce referrals (2016–2022). Much of this conduct predates CD&R's 2022 acquisition (Kindred at Home / Humana era).

businesses.name: Greystar
businesses.platform_company: Largest US apartment manager: ~1M units under management, ~141,000 owned; vertically integrated investment manager and operator

evidence.description: Named in the DOJ's RealPage rent-algorithm case; Greystar (the nation's largest apartment manager) agreed in Aug 2025 to stop setting rents using RealPage's software and to stop sharing competitively sensitive data with competitors.

businesses.name: Grindr
businesses.firm_name: San Vicente Acquisition (Ray Zage / Tiga, James Lu / Joffre Capital)
businesses.platform_company: Grindr Inc. (NYSE: GRND). Bought out of Beijing Kunlun Tech ownership in 2020 under a CFIUS divestiture order, taken public via SPAC in November 2022, still majority-controlled by Ray Zage and James Lu

evidence.description: The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States determined in 2019 that Beijing Kunlun Tech's ownership of Grindr was a national security risk, on the reasoning that the app's data on users, including location and health information, could be used for blackmail or coercion, and ordered a divestiture. Kunlun sold its stake for about $608 million in 2020 under a June 2020 CFIUS deadline.

Norway's Datatilsynet fined Grindr NOK 65 million in December 2021, its largest fine ever, for unlawfully disclosing user data to advertising partners. The regulator found the consents Grindr collected were neither voluntary, specific nor informed, and that because being a Grindr user implicitly reveals sexual orientation, the disclosures involved a special category of personal data. The Privacy Appeals Board upheld the decision in 2023 and the Court of Appeal upheld it again in 2025.

The Norwegian Consumer Council's January 2020 'Out of Control' report found Grindr transmitted GPS location, IP address, age and gender to a large number of advertising and behavioural-profiling third parties. The report was the basis for the complaint that produced the Datatilsynet fine.

In October 2025 majority holders Ray Zage and James Lu explored taking Grindr private at a roughly $3 billion valuation, after a lender called loans the two had taken against their shares, and later raised the offer to $18.00 per share. Grindr's special committee ceased engagement with the proposal on November 26, 2025, citing uncertainty over the financing.

businesses.name: Havenpark Communities
businesses.platform_company: Utah-based operator of manufactured-housing communities across the Midwest and South

evidence.description: In 2019 Havenpark raised lot rents 24–69% at its Iowa parks (one resident's rent rose ~60%), prompting Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Dave Loebsack to write the company calling the practices predatory. Residents have since reported neglected conditions (including a park sinking due to water erosion), and Havenpark has been selling off its Iowa parks amid ongoing complaints.

businesses.name: HCR ManorCare
businesses.platform_company: Then the 2nd-largest US nursing-home chain; after Carlyle's LBO collapsed it was acquired out of 2018 bankruptcy by ProMedica (a nonprofit)

evidence.description: Carlyle took HCR ManorCare private in 2007 for $6.3B, three-quarters funded by debt. A 2011 sale-leaseback sold the company's real estate for $6.1B (recouping Carlyle's ~$1.3B equity) but left the chain paying rent it increasingly couldn't afford. It filed for bankruptcy in March 2018.

As ManorCare cut costs and laid off staff, health-code violations rose 26% between 2013 and 2017. State inspectors found residents left unattended: call buttons so poorly staffed that some residents regularly soiled themselves waiting for help to the bathroom (Washington Post investigation).

businesses.name: Heartland Dental
businesses.platform_company: Largest US DSO: 1,900+ affiliated practices across 39 states + DC; Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan retains a minority stake

businesses.name: Homes of America
businesses.platform_company: Manufactured-housing subsidiary of Alden Global Capital, the hedge fund known for aggressive cost-cutting at local newspapers

evidence.description: Homes of America (Alden Global Capital) was named in both Sen. Warren's March 2026 corporate-landlord probe and Sen. Maggie Hassan's Dec 2025 Joint Economic Committee investigation into manufactured-housing owners over affordability and resident living-conditions concerns.

businesses.name: Hub International
businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US insurance brokerages; a buy-and-build rollup that has acquired hundreds of agencies. Recorded as an ownership fact: 'who really owns your insurance broker.'

businesses.name: iHeartMedia
businesses.platform_company: Largest US radio broadcaster (~850 stations); taken private by Bain Capital and Thomas H. Lee Partners in 2008, now publicly traded after its 2019 restructuring

evidence.description: Bain Capital and Thomas H. Lee Partners took Clear Channel (later iHeartMedia) private in a 2008 leveraged buyout valued at ~$26.7B, loading the largest US radio company with debt that ballooned from ~$8B to more than $20B. Unable to service it, iHeartMedia filed for Chapter 11 in 2018 (one of the largest media bankruptcies ever) while the PE firms nearly broke even through discounted debt purchases and management fees.

businesses.name: Impact Communities
businesses.platform_company: Manufactured-housing communities operated by Frank Rolfe & Dave Reynolds, who teach investors a buy-and-raise-lot-rent strategy via 'Mobile Home University'

evidence.description: Impact Communities (run by Frank Rolfe and Dave Reynolds, who teach investors via 'Mobile Home University' to buy parks and raise lot rents on residents who own their homes but not the land) was named in Sen. Warren's March 2026 corporate-landlord probe.

businesses.name: Invitation Homes
businesses.platform_company: The largest US single-family landlord; created by Blackstone in 2012 after the foreclosure crisis, taken public in 2017, and fully exited by Blackstone by ~2019 (now NYSE: INVH)

evidence.description: FTC settlement ($48M, Sept 2024): the FTC charged Invitation Homes with deceiving renters on price, charging undisclosed 'junk fees' (mandatory monthly charges for smart-home tech and air-filter delivery costing up to ~$1,700/yr), withholding security deposits (returned in only ~40% of cases vs. a ~64% norm), and unfair eviction practices, including steering pandemic-era renters away from the CDC declaration that would have protected them from eviction. Invitation paid $48M in consumer refunds (no admission of wrongdoing). Blackstone founded and ran the company 2012–2019; the FTC's conduct period spans 2018–2023.

businesses.name: LivCor
businesses.platform_company: Blackstone's apartment platform; Blackstone is the largest US apartment owner (~230,000 units)

evidence.description: Named in the DOJ's Jan 2025 amended RealPage complaint as one of six large landlords that coordinated rents through RealPage's algorithm. Blackstone's LivCor settled with the DOJ in Dec 2025, agreeing to stop using revenue-management software that relies on competitors' sensitive data and to cooperate in the ongoing litigation.

businesses.name: Main Street Renewal
businesses.platform_company: Amherst's single-family rental platform: roughly 16,000 homes across the Midwest and Sunbelt

businesses.name: McClatchy
businesses.platform_company: 2nd-largest US newspaper chain: 30 papers including the Miami Herald, Sacramento Bee, Kansas City Star and Charlotte Observer

evidence.description: McClatchy carried heavy debt from its $4.5B 2006 purchase of Knight-Ridder and filed for Chapter 11 in Feb 2020. Hedge fund Chatham Asset Management, its longtime lead lender, won the bankruptcy auction in July 2020, ending 163 years of family control and handing the chain to its creditors.

businesses.name: MediaNews Group
businesses.platform_company: Alden's flagship newspaper group (formerly Digital First Media): Denver Post, San Jose Mercury News, St. Paul Pioneer Press, Boston Herald and dozens more; Alden controls 200+ US papers

evidence.description: After taking over MediaNews Group out of bankruptcy in 2010, Alden cut newsroom staffing by more than 75% across its papers, and its 2016 consolidation of eight San Francisco Bay Area papers into two triggered mass layoffs. Alden's playbook (gutting newsrooms and selling off real estate) was the subject of The Atlantic's 2021 cover story 'The Men Who Are Killing America's Newspapers.'

businesses.name: Mission Pet Health
businesses.platform_company: Southern Veterinary Partners + Mission Veterinary Partners; co-owned with Shore Capital

businesses.name: Nine West
businesses.platform_company: Footwear/apparel maker (formerly the Jones Group); Sycamore's 2014 LBO; filed for bankruptcy in 2018

evidence.description: Sycamore acquired the Jones Group in a 2014 LBO, renamed it Nine West, and moved its most valuable brands (Stuart Weitzman, Kurt Geiger, Jones Apparel) to Sycamore affiliates for below fair value (beyond creditors' reach) while loading Nine West with debt. Nine West went bankrupt in 2018; in the litigation that followed, a court found the former directors may have breached their fiduciary duty by failing to evaluate whether the LBO would render the company insolvent, a landmark warning about PE buyout structures.

businesses.name: ParshipMeet Group / The Meet Group (MeetMe, Skout, Tagged, LOVOO)
businesses.platform_company: The Meet Group (MeetMe, Skout, Tagged, growlr) was taken private in 2020 for about $500 million by NuCom Group, the joint venture between ProSiebenSat.1 and General Atlantic, and merged with Parship Group to form ParshipMeet Group. ProSiebenSat.1 agreed in March 2025 to buy out General Atlantic's minority stakes, making it the sole owner

evidence.description: General Atlantic's five-year investment ended on March 20, 2025, when ProSiebenSat.1 approved an agreement to acquire General Atlantic's minority stakes in both NuCom Group and ParshipMeet Group, alongside an intended sale of Verivox. Recorded as an ownership fact: the apps changed hands twice without their users being party to either transaction.

businesses.name: Progress Residential
businesses.platform_company: Largest US institutional single-family landlord (~94,000 homes as of 2025), including scattered-site and build-to-rent

evidence.description: Progress charges an array of fees on top of rent (e.g., a $200 eviction-administration fee, a $75 maintenance-visit fee, per-pet fees, and a 10% late fee) and has been an aggressive evictor, filing on tenants only a single month behind. Congress investigated whether Progress and peers filed evictions during the pandemic moratorium, and Sen. Sherrod Brown questioned why its pandemic-era eviction filings fell disproportionately on majority-Black communities. Tenants formed a 3,000+ member 'Victims of Progress Residential' group citing lost deposits, fees, and unaddressed maintenance.

businesses.name: RealPage
businesses.platform_company: Apartment revenue-management / pricing software (YieldStar, AI Revenue Management) used by landlords nationwide, not a landlord itself but the pricing engine at the center of the DOJ rent-algorithm case

evidence.description: The DOJ and eight state attorneys general sued RealPage in Aug 2024, alleging its YieldStar / AI revenue-management software let competing landlords share nonpublic, competitively sensitive pricing and occupancy data and algorithmically align their rents, an unlawful price-fixing scheme the DOJ said harmed millions of renters. RealPage settled in Nov 2025, agreeing to stop enabling the sharing of competitors' nonpublic pricing data and to stop training its pricing AI on it. Thoma Bravo acquired RealPage in 2021 for ~$10.2B.

businesses.name: Red Lobster
businesses.platform_company: Casual-dining seafood chain; Golden Gate bought it from Darden in 2014, later sold it on; filed Chapter 11 in May 2024

evidence.description: To help finance its $2.1B 2014 purchase of Red Lobster from Darden, Golden Gate Capital sold the chain's real estate for ~$1.5B in a sale-leaseback, pocketing cash while saddling Red Lobster with rent obligations it couldn't sustain. That debt-and-rent burden was widely cited as a key driver of Red Lobster's May 2024 Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

businesses.name: RHP Properties
businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US manufactured-housing owners (~370 communities); Brookfield acquired 135 RHP parks in 2017, RHP retaining ~5% and managing operations

evidence.description: Named in Sen. Elizabeth Warren's March 2026 probe of the biggest corporate landlords across the single-family, multifamily and manufactured-housing sectors over allegedly aggressive and predatory rent and fee practices.

businesses.name: SCP Health
businesses.platform_company: 4th-largest US emergency-medicine staffing firm (~258 emergency departments; 7,500+ clinicians across 36 states)

businesses.name: Sears
businesses.platform_company: Once ~3,500 stores; controlled by Eddie Lampert's ESL since the 2005 Kmart–Sears merger, now reduced to a handful under the ESL-controlled Transformco

evidence.description: Sears' post-bankruptcy estate sued Eddie Lampert and ESL alleging they stripped more than $2B of assets from the retailer via self-dealing (including the Lands' End spinoff and the 2015 Seritage sale-leaseback of 200+ Sears stores), moving value beyond creditors' reach as the company slid toward its Oct 2018 bankruptcy. The claims settled for $175M. Sears shrank from ~3,500 stores to a handful.

businesses.name: Sila Services
businesses.platform_company: 30+ HVAC/plumbing/electrical brands across the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest; acquired from Morgan Stanley Capital Partners

businesses.name: Smile Brands
businesses.platform_company: 75+ affiliated brands including Affordable Care; Gryphon re-acquired the DSO in 2024

businesses.name: Sound Physicians
businesses.platform_company: Hospitalist + emergency-medicine staffing; 2018 ~$2.15B buyout led by Summit Partners with Optum (UnitedHealth), Revelstoke and Silversmith

businesses.name: Spark Networks (Zoosk, JDate, ChristianMingle, EliteSingles)
businesses.platform_company: Spark Networks SE / Spark Networks Services GmbH, operator of Zoosk, JDate, ChristianMingle, EliteSingles and SilverSingles. Taken over in full by funds managed by private credit manager MGG Investment Group in a January 2024 German StaRUG restructuring

evidence.description: MGG Investment Group, already a principal creditor, became Spark Networks' sole equity owner in January 2024 after a German court approved a StaRUG restructuring plan that eliminated more than $45 million of debt and wiped out the existing shareholders. It was the first StaRUG plan recognized by a US court under Chapter 15.

The 2024 restructuring did not hold. After MGG, its main lender, withdrew funding, a Berlin court placed Spark Networks Services GmbH under preliminary insolvency administration in mid-January 2026, and the company filed for Chapter 15 in the United States to have the German proceeding recognized. Spark said it intends to sell its assets while continuing to operate, leaving paying subscribers of Zoosk, JDate and ChristianMingle exposed to an asset sale.

businesses.name: Sports Authority
businesses.platform_company: Sporting-goods retailer; Leonard Green's 2006 $1.3B LBO; liquidated ~450 stores in 2016

evidence.description: Leonard Green & Partners bought Sports Authority in a 2006 LBO for ~$1.3B, loading it with debt. After missing a debt payment in early 2016, the retailer filed for Chapter 11 in March 2016 and liquidated all ~450 stores. It is one of several Leonard Green retail bankruptcies, alongside J.Crew and Joann.

businesses.name: TeamHealth
businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US emergency-medicine and hospital physician staffing firms

evidence.description: ProPublica documented how TeamHealth, under Blackstone, used out-of-network emergency-room billing to mark up patient bills, a model that generated large surprise bills for insured patients who had no choice of ER physician.

US DOJ False Claims Act settlement ($60M, 2017): TeamHealth, as successor to IPC Healthcare, resolved allegations of 'upcoding': billing Medicare, Medicaid, the Defense Health Agency and the federal employee program for higher and more expensive levels of service than were actually provided. Originated as a qui tam whistleblower suit; TeamHealth entered a 5-year Corporate Integrity Agreement.

businesses.name: Thrive Pet Healthcare
businesses.platform_company: formerly Pathway Vet Alliance

businesses.name: Toys R Us
businesses.platform_company: Iconic toy retailer; taken private in a 2005 $6.6B LBO by Bain Capital, KKR and Vornado Realty Trust; liquidated in 2018

evidence.description: Bain Capital, KKR and Vornado took Toys R Us private in a 2005 $6.6B leveraged buyout, loading it with ~$5B of debt that cost ~$400M/year to service. The company filed for Chapter 11 in Sept 2017 and liquidated in 2018 (closing ~800 stores and cutting 33,000 jobs, initially with no severance) even as the PE owners collected ~$464M in fees and interest. Congress publicly confronted Bain and KKR over the collapse.

businesses.name: Treehouse Communities
businesses.platform_company: Blackstone's manufactured-housing platform

evidence.description: Blackstone was named in Sen. Elizabeth Warren's March 2026 probe of the 14 biggest corporate landlords over allegedly predatory rent and fee practices across the housing sector, including manufactured housing.

businesses.name: Tribune Publishing
businesses.platform_company: Chicago Tribune, New York Daily News, Orlando Sentinel, Hartford Courant and more (Baltimore Sun later sold); Alden bought Tribune Publishing for $633M in 2021

evidence.description: After Alden's $633M takeover of Tribune Publishing in 2021, papers such as the Chicago Tribune quickly lost about a quarter of their newsroom to buyouts, thinning coverage of state and local government. Sens. Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth publicly pressed Alden over the 'alarming' staff cuts.

businesses.name: Tricon Residential
businesses.platform_company: ~40,000 US homes; Blackstone took Tricon private in May 2024 for ~$3.5B, its return to single-family rentals and now its primary US SFR platform (it also absorbed the wound-down Home Partners of America)

businesses.name: TurnPoint Services
businesses.platform_company: HVAC/plumbing/electrical platform; brands include Southern Home Services; acquired from Trivest Partners

businesses.name: VetCor
businesses.platform_company: co-owned with Harvest Partners and Cressey & Company

businesses.name: Vice Media
businesses.platform_company: Digital media company (Vice, Vice News, Motherboard) once valued at ~$5.7B

evidence.description: Vice Media filed for Chapter 11 in May 2023 and was sold for ~$350M to a lender group led by Fortress Investment Group (with Soros Fund Management and Monroe Capital). The new owners shuttered Vice World News, canceled the flagship Vice News Tonight, and later closed Vice.com's newsroom, cutting hundreds of jobs.

businesses.name: Western Dental / Sonrava Health
businesses.platform_company: Rebranded Sonrava Health; one of the longest-held PE dental platforms (since 2012); a 2024 sale process did not complete

businesses.name: Wrench Group
businesses.platform_company: 25+ HVAC/plumbing/electrical brands; minority co-investors TSG Consumer Partners, Oak Hill Capital, AustralianSuper, Crescent Capital

businesses.name: YES! Communities
businesses.platform_company: ~265 communities / 75,000+ home sites in 24 states; majority-owned since 2016 by a JV led by Singapore's GIC (with PSERS), Stockbridge retaining ~29%

evidence.description: Named among the manufactured-housing landlords in Sen. Elizabeth Warren's March 2026 probe of the biggest corporate landlords over allegedly predatory rent and fee practices, and cited in reporting on aggressive rent increases across large mobile-home operators.
